messages:
Morgan: FYI, customer ACME reports the monthly tokens showed as refilled in the Console at 00:00 local, but their service immediately got 429s when the long-running streaming client reconnected. They say UI=full but API says 0. Sigh. 
Devon: Do we have repro steps or a tenant id? Is this Dedicated or Hosted?
Morgan: Hosted (standard plan). Tenant: acme-corp. Repro steps they gave: 1) Open longstream session before reset, keep it idle 2) At reset window they see UI go from 0 -> full 3) client reconnects -> immediate 429s. They pasted a curl showing header: `X-Quota-Remaining: 0` while the Console shows ~1M tokens.
Devon: Can you paste the curl/log snippet? Curious whether the token bucket refreshed server-side or if a cache layer still has pre-refresh state.
Morgan: Snippet: ```bash
curl -i -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-***" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
X-Quota-Remaining: 0
X-Quota-Reset: 1719993600
```
Morgan: They also noted they're in PST (UTC-8). UI shows refill at 00:00 PST; backend logs show job at 00:00 UTC.
Elena: Billing ledger shows the monthly allotment credited at 2026-03-10T00:00:02Z and the promo top-up at 2026-03-10T00:00:05Z. Both hits processed by the billing worker, but the quota assignment job to the serving cache is a separate async task. Could be a race with the streaming session reattach.
Anita: Can we check the quota refresh job trace for acme-corp and the serving cache invalidation order? If longstream session resumed before cache invalidation propagated, the gateway might still be consulting stale Redis token counts.
quota-bot: [system] quota_refresh_job: id=qr_20260310_000002 tenant=acme-corp status=completed shards_updated=2 propagate_ts=2026-03-10T00:00:10Z
Devon: Ah — propagate_ts is 8s after job completion. If client reconnected in that window, edge nodes might still report old counters. Need to see if we return stale headers in that window.
Morgan: Customer timeline: UI refresh at 16:00 PST (00:00 UTC), client reattach at 16:00:03 PST (00:00:03 UTC). They got 429s for ~6s until edge headers changed.
Elena: That lines up with billing being fast but serving-side propagation lagging (cache propagation 6-10s). We should communicate transient refill visibility and advise reattempt/backoff on reconnect.
Devon: For mitigation: (1) make quota refresh atomic for tenant (apply to serving cache then update ledger) or (2) have the gateway accept tokens from the new ledger if propagate_ts > conn_ts. Both need infra change. Short term: docs + support guidance + escalate to infra for a fix.
Anita: I can add a short-lived workaround: if a reconnect occurs within 30s after a tenant's refresh event, treat the request as eligible and check ledger as the source of truth. But that requires careful rate-limit race handling.
Morgan: Customer asked for ETA. Can we promise some immediate mitigation? They have a bursty workload and the >6s outage killed their demo.
Devon: I'll open an infra task and mark P2 with a customer-impact tag. In parallel: Morgan please tell ACME to retry on reconnect with exponential backoff for ~30s and we'll prioritize a fix. Also capture traces for acme-corp for 00:00 UTC window.
Morgan: Copy. I'll send the suggested messaging and collect trace IDs. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
Devon: Also adding a debugging command for support: ```bash
# check tenant refresh metadata
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-internal" https://internal.redwood.ai/v1/admin/tenants/acme-corp/refresh
# response excerpts
{"last_refresh":"2026-03-10T00:00:02Z","propagate_ts":"2026-03-10T00:00:10Z","shards_updated":2}
```
Anita: I'll look at edge cache invalidation logs and post findings here.
quota-bot: [system] follow-up: infra-ticket=INF-8742 created by Devon
Morgan: I'll update the customer with retry/backoff guidance + note that we see a propagation lag window ~<10s.
Devon: Thanks. Closing interim until infra updates.
